chapter: The Legends of Jazz and life on the road
title: The car accident in Michigan
summary: Driving alone to a concert in snow he crashes, is taken to the theater, forbidden to play, and learns he has a concussion.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: We got into Detroit that night after changing at Atlanta, about six or seven o'clock. Then we had to get a car. Our first date was a little town 150 miles north of Detroit--I'll get to that later. So we stopped at Lansing, Michigan--that's the capital--spend the night there. So for some reason or another, he decided he would drive his car, 150 miles to Lansing I knew a lot of people in

Lansing from my home town, so I rented a car for myself, get to get around for myself. So that night I had the car and I had to turn it back the next day, I said instead of riding all jammed up with the rest of the guys I'd just drive my own car, and so I did.
They all left me in my hotel room and one of the dancers came up and asked me if I was all right and I said yes. I said I'll see you a little later and they left ahead of me.

So I got in my car and started driving; I had the directions and I found myself getting sleepy, so I stopped. I got a sandwich and two cups of coffee, and I don't drink coffee in the evening. So I started out again and I got lost and I came all the way back, about fifty miles back, to try and find my way straight again.
I finally got myself all straight again and it was getting almost dark now, and
we were due to play at eight o'clock and it was almost six o'clock now.

So I started driving and I was travelling pretty fast I guess and finally I got on a little narrow road and it was snowing, snow was on both sides and I hit a snowbank. I didn't know but when I woke up, some passerby had picked me out of the car.

They said what happened was I swerved this way, back this way and back this way and backed up into the snowbank, against the snowbank and I was asleep, still unconscious. Some passerbys came and pulled me out of the car, and they saw who I was--Oh, you're with the group that's going to play, well, we're on our way to the concert.' I said, 'What happened? Where am I?' They said, 'You're in Mighican.' 'What am I doing in Michigan?' I was out, you see.
Anyway they took me onto the theater. When we got to the theater the
boss was looking for me because it was about five minutes to eight.
I told him about my accident and he said are you ready to go on and I said I'm ready and he said you ain't ready to go on, you're going to the hospital. He would not let me play.

The manager--it was Floyd Turnham's girlfriend, she travelled with him, she took me to the hospital and they examined me from head to toe. I got a bill for it. They said there was nothing seriously wrong, I had a little bleeding on my lungs or something like that. I had a couple bumps on my head, which was a concussion.
Do you think that might have been the result of--
Wait a minute. That's the cause of it.
Anyway the x-ray then didn't show it, but the doctor told me it's liable to show up later.
So we came home after that and I made another tour. This is February 22 when the accident happened. Two weeks later is when I fell out of bed. It was a concussion.
